notes: Miami is hard without a car: rent one for the Everglades and Key Biscayne, and use Uber/Lyft for South Beach, Wynwood and Little Havana; Metromover is free.
June to November is hurricane season, with 33°C heat, humidity and an hour of rain every afternoon: swim in the morning, visit museums or malls in the afternoon, and go out in the evening.
Cuban coffee (cafecito) costs 2 USD from a ventanita; Cuban sandwiches, croquetas and ropa vieja in Little Havana cost 15-25 USD.
Tip 18-20% (some places add it to the bill automatically, so don't tip twice); sunbeds on beaches cost 30-50 USD.
Sunscreen and water are essential; UV is very high at midday.
Book your Everglades airboat tour 2-3 days ahead; alligators are most active in the morning.

stops.name: Ocean Drive Art Deco
stops.tips: Pastel Art Deco hotels; best in morning light, plus the Versace mansion (Casa Casuarina).

stops.name: South Beach
stops.tips: Swim early in the morning (33°C) and look for shade after 11:00; expect a downpour in the afternoon.

stops.name: Puerto Sagua Restaurant
stops.tips: A Cuban diner since 1962; try the ropa vieja (shredded beef stew) and café con leche in South Beach.

stops.name: Española Way
stops.tips: A Mediterranean-style pedestrian street lined with cafes.

stops.name: South Pointe Park
stops.tips: A park and pier at the tip of the island; watch ships pass and catch the sunset.

backups.name: Joe's Stone Crab
backups.tips: Serving stone crab since 1913 (October to May); at South Pointe.

backups.name: Wolfsonian FIU
backups.tips: A museum of Art Deco design; a good rainy-day option.

stops.name: Wynwood Walls
stops.tips: The world's best-known street art garden; buy tickets online, the surrounding streets are free.

stops.name: Wynwood Street Art Tour
stops.tips: Murals along NW 2nd Ave, plus galleries.

stops.name: Coyo Taco Wynwood
stops.tips: Mexican street tacos, with a hidden bar in the back room.

stops.name: Design District
stops.tips: Luxury shops and public art (the Buckminster Fuller dome); ICA Miami is free.

stops.name: Institute of Contemporary Art Miami
stops.tips: Free contemporary art in the Design District.

backups.name: Zak the Baker Wynwood
backups.tips: An award-winning sourdough bakery; an alternative to tacos.

backups.name: Pérez Art Museum Miami
backups.tips: A museum on the bay with hanging gardens.

stops.name: Calle Ocho
stops.tips: SW 8th Street: rooster statues, cigar shops and salsa.

stops.name: Domino Park Máximo Gómez
stops.tips: A park where older men play dominoes; ask permission before taking photos.

stops.name: Ball & Chain
stops.tips: A salsa club dating from 1935; come at lunchtime for a mojito and empanada, with live music.

stops.name: Versailles Restaurant
stops.tips: The world's best-known Cuban restaurant (1971); order a cafecito (small sweet espresso) from the ventanita (walk-up window), plus croquetas and vaca frita (crispy shredded beef).

stops.name: Azucar Ice Cream
stops.tips: Cuban ice cream; try the Abuela María flavour.

backups.name: El Pub Restaurant
backups.tips: Cuban sandwiches; go here if the queue at Versailles is long.

backups.name: Cubaocho Museum
backups.tips: Cuban art and a rum bar; an alternative to Ball & Chain.

stops.name: Vizcaya Museum and Gardens
stops.tips: A 1916 Italian-style villa with gardens on the bay; cooler in the morning, closed on Tuesdays.

stops.name: Coconut Grove
stops.tips: A neighbourhood of banyan trees, with CocoWalk.

stops.name: GreenStreet Cafe
stops.tips: A Coconut Grove brunch classic with a terrace.

stops.name: Crandon Park, Key Biscayne
stops.tips: Swim after the afternoon downpour; there is shade.

stops.name: Bill Baggs Cape Florida Lighthouse
stops.tips: A lighthouse and beach; come for sunset.

backups.name: Rusty Pelican Key Biscayne
backups.tips: Seafood with views over the bay.

backups.name: Fairchild Tropical Botanic Garden
backups.tips: A tropical garden; an alternative to the beach.

stops.name: Everglades Safari Park
stops.tips: 45 minutes from Miami (by car or tour); take an airboat tour (about 42 USD) to see alligators and sawgrass, cooler in the morning.

stops.name: Shark Valley Tram
stops.tips: A 24 km tram ride or bike route in the national park; there is an observation tower, and alligators along the way.

stops.name: Robert Is Here Fruit Stand
stops.tips: A tropical fruit stand in Homestead; try the key lime milkshake.

stops.name: Coral Castle
stops.tips: A castle of coral rock carved by one man, in Homestead.

stops.name: Bayside Marketplace
stops.tips: A waterfront market; boat tours leave from here.

stops.name: Biscayne Bay Boat Tour
stops.tips: Millionaires' islands and the city skyline; 90 minutes.

stops.name: Brickell City Centre
stops.tips: A shopping mall in the financial district; air-conditioned.

stops.name: La Mar by Gastón Acurio
stops.tips: Peruvian cuisine at the Mandarin Oriental; try the ceviche and enjoy the bay views.

stops.name: Brickell Key Promenade
stops.tips: A waterfront path around the island; sunset and skyscrapers.

backups.name: CVI.CHE 105 Downtown
backups.tips: Peruvian ceviche at a lower price.

backups.name: Frost Science Museum
backups.tips: An aquarium and planetarium; a good rainy-day option.

stops.name: Lincoln Road Mall
stops.tips: A pedestrian shopping street; grab a coffee and last souvenirs.

stops.name: Miami Beach Boardwalk
stops.tips: A wooden seafront path from 21st to 46th Street; your last look at the sea.

stops.name: Yardbird Southern Table
stops.tips: Southern cooking: fried chicken and waffles for a farewell meal.

stops.name: Miami International Airport Metrorail
stops.tips: 20 minutes to the airport; time to say goodbye.

backups.name: La Sandwicherie Miami Beach
backups.tips: French-style sandwiches for a quick farewell bite.

backups.name: Bass Museum of Art
backups.tips: Miami Beach's art museum; an alternative to the boardwalk.
